judged_text: The blacklist lowercases its configured entries (line 71) but compares them against non-lowercased guest input (line 77), so no mixed-case spelling of a blacklisted address can ever match. An operator who sets BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS=bad@example.com watches 'Bad@example.com' get persisted as an attendee and emailed the full booking ICS including location and video link — the blocklist control is dead for any input containing a single uppercase character.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is normalized to lowercase (`split(...).map(email => email.toLowerCase())`), but the comparison uses the raw `guest` string: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Since `guest` is not lowercased (nor otherwise normalized) before `includes`, any mixed/upper-case variant of a blacklisted email (e.g. `Bad@example.com`) will not match and will pass through to be persisted and emailed.
